title: Orsen and the Static Revisited
premise: Casper Amberdale, a veteran navigator hauling freight through contested orbits, carries a secret: the hold of her ship, the Orsen, is packed with memory backups of people she could not save twenty years ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries — the tongue of the colony fleet her backups came from — Casper discovers a survivor has been revived from a stolen backup and both fleets now believe the other committed the original massacre. To prevent a war that will destroy the jump corridor home, Casper must sustain a fabricated translation that pins the massacre on a third party, even as the revived survivor's memories begin to contradict her lie. In the end, Casper chooses truth over survival: she confesses her role in abandoning the colony, releases the backups to public record, and holds the two fleets apart long enough for the jump window to close on peace instead of war.
about_author: Quentin Sterling is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. Sterling writes about the quiet debts survivors carry, drawing on a family history of colonial resettlement programs.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hauling ore through contested orbits, Casper intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct for two hundred years — the language of the Meridian colony fleet whose backups sleep in her hold. She recognizes it instantly and lies to her crew about what it says. Beat: dread reawakened.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, flashback-woven. We learn the Orsen's cargo bay hides forty-one memory cores she rescued after the Meridian massacre, cores she was ordered to jettison and didn't. Her engineer Tam questions the power draw. Beat: guilt made physical.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Corridor
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The signal's origin sits between the Concord blockade and the Remnant flotilla, both fleets massing around the last stable jump window of the season. Casper calculates she can slip through if she moves within six days. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest Lies
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers the hold's hidden power taps and confronts Casper, who claims the cores are salvage awaiting sale. Tam agrees to stay silent but starts his own investigation into their origin tags. Beat: fragile trust.

chapters.title: What the Signal Said
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Deciphering more of the transmission, Casper realizes it isn't a distress call at all — it's an accusation, naming the Concord fleet as the massacre's perpetrator. Someone alive wrote it. Beat: the past is not finished.

chapters.title: Boarding at Brink Station
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At a neutral station, a Concord intelligence officer, Ilsa Vey, offers Casper a contract: translate the signal for them. Casper accepts, planning to control whatever story emerges. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: The Revived
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV introduced. Aboard the Remnant flotilla, Sefa Kell wakes from a backup revival with fragmented memories of the massacre night — memories that include a rescue ship that fled without answering hails. The Orsen. Beat: the witness awakens.

chapters.title: Translation as Weaponry
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Vey demands a full translation; Casper delivers one subtly doctored to implicate a defunct pirate syndicate as third-party attackers. The fabrication buys calm — for now. Beat: the lie takes shape.

chapters.title: Memories That Contradict
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa's restored memories sharpen: she remembers the fleeing ship's registry prefix, and she remembers voices — children — still aboard when it jumped. She presses the Remnant council to hunt the ship down. Beat: the noose tightens.

chapters.title: Tam Finds the Tags
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam traces the core serial numbers to the Meridian colony's official evacuation roster — forty-one names listed as 'abandoned, presumed lost.' He realizes Casper stole them from a war-crimes evidence lockup. Beat: betrayal and awe entwined.

chapters.title: Intercepted Mid-Jump Approach
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Orsen is caught in a Concord interdiction net near the corridor. Vey boards, finds nothing — but plants a tracker, and mentions casually that the Remnants have revived a witness. Casper understands her lie has a deadline. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Witness Names the Ship
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Under Remnant questioning, Sefa identifies the fleeing vessel by its drive signature. The Remnant flotilla alters course toward the corridor — directly across the Orsen's path. Beat: convergence.

chapters.title: A Lie Held by Two Hands
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper transmits her doctored translation to the Remnants anonymously, hoping to stall them. It half-works: they pause, but demand the 'rescue ship' surrender for verification. Every hour costs fuel she doesn't have. Beat: the price compounds.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam decrypts the final core — core zero — and finds Casper's own backup, recorded the night of the massacre. Confronting her, he learns she fled because command jammed her comms and threatened to space her crew. Beat: sympathy reframes judgment.

chapters.title: Vey's Real Assignment
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Vey reveals to her superiors that the Concord knew the massacre was its own rogue squadron's doing; her job is ensuring the translation never proves it. She suspects Casper's version is false — and useful anyway. Beat: institutional rot exposed.

chapters.title: Rendezvous at the Window
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Both fleets converge on the jump corridor as the window opens in thirty hours. Casper broadcasts a parley offer in the extinct language, speaking directly to Sefa: meet me, and I'll give you the forty-one. Beat: gambit.

chapters.title: Face to Face with Memory
chapters.summary: Alternating Casper/Sefa POV. Aboard the neutral station, Sefa hears Casper's confession — the flight, the jammed comms, the twenty years of carrying the dead. Sefa's rage cracks into grief: Casper is the only other person who remembers Meridian. Beat: catharsis through confrontation.

chapters.title: The Fabrication Unravels
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Concord analysts expose inconsistencies in Casper's translation; Vey is ordered to seize the Orsen and arrest both women before the window closes. War posture spreads through both fleets. Beat: everything Casper built collapses.

chapters.title: Core Zero Broadcast
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Out of options, Casper does the unthinkable: she uploads all forty-two cores — including her own backup and its embedded command logs proving the jamming order — to both fleets' open channels. Truth as her last weapon. Beat: sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. As evidence floods both fleets, officers waver; Vey refuses her arrest order and stands down her squadron; Sefa testifies that vengeance against one navigator won't resurrect anyone. The jump window closes on two fleets that chose, barely, not to fire. Beat: peace snatched from the brink.

chapters.title: Forty-One Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Weeks later, at a joint memorial, Sefa and Casper read the forty-one names into the record, restoring the Meridian dead to history. Tam takes the navigator's chair beside Casper. Beat: mourning becomes belonging.

chapters.title: Orsen, Underway
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Orsen departs under a joint escort contract, its hold finally empty and humming clean. Casper still hears static some nights — but now it sounds like company rather than accusation. Beat: survival's price paid, found family aboard.
